findings.no_iteration_bound: Nothing in the body bounds any iteration count: there is no counter field, no increment anywhere in the body, and no backward branch except jumps to the shared epilogue at 0x5cdf317. Per dispatcher-loop iteration the tail call therefore returns non-null whenever the key is live, and the loop at head 0x2ae1974 can be left through this call only after the key's destructor glue has run on the dispatcher's thread (state 2).
findings.null_vs_nonnull: The getter returns the cell pointer itself (never the value pointer) in exactly two cases: the entry state byte is 1 (live), or it is 0 and initialisation completes (adoption of a non-null *rsi, or allocation of a fresh 0x28-byte value). It returns null in exactly one case: the entry state byte is neither 0 nor 1 -- in practice 2, the destroyed state the destructor glue 0x5cdf3e0 stores before dropping the value. Allocation failure and a racing reloaded state other than 0 or 1 do not return at all: they diverge through the allocation-failure slot 0x64df490 and the std unreachable panic slot 0x64df730.
findings.reads_writes: Fast paths (state 1, or state other than 0/1) read only the state byte and write nothing. The only locked operation in the body is that single lock dec at 0x5cdf37f.
